chunks: [A part of the same sermon About the Consultative Committee after the death of ‘Umar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb :]

Someone [1] said to me, “O son of Abī Ṭālib, you are eager for the caliphate.” Then I told him: “Rather, you are, by Allāh, more greedy, although more remote, while I am more suited as well as nearer. I have demanded it as my right, while you are intervening between me and it, and you are turning my face from it.” When I knocked at his ears with arguments among the crowd of those present he was startled as if he was stunned not knowing what reply to give me about it.

key_terms.ابْن أَبِي طَالِب: Son of Abu Talib (a title for Imam Ali)
key_terms.يَوْمِ الشُّورَى: The Consultative Committee (Shura) after the death of Umar

ai.seo_question: What was Imam Ali's response to the claim that he was greedy for the caliphate?
ai.summary: This passage captures the pivotal moment of the *Yawm al-Shura* (Day of Consultation), where Imam Ali (AS) refutes the claim of personal ambition by asserting his inherent right (*Haqq*) based on proximity to the Prophet and divine designation, contrasting it with the political obstruction of the companions. The rhetorical climax highlights the opponents' speechlessness (*Hubt*) when confronted with irrefutable proof in the presence of the elite, underscoring the Shia view that the caliphate was a divine trust rather than a political prize contested by the eager.
